html:
Michael the Brave was prince of Wallachia from 1593 to 1601, who briefly ruled Wallachia, Transylvania and Moldavia together in 1600, the first time the three lands later forming Romania had one ruler.

He joined a Christian league against the Ottomans, killed his Ottoman creditors in Bucharest and won the Battle of Călugăreni in 1595. In 1599 he took Transylvania, and in 1600 Moldavia. His rule fell apart within months as the Transylvanian nobles and the Poles turned on him. Seeking help from the Habsburg emperor, he was murdered in his camp near Turda in August 1601 by men of the Habsburg general Giorgio Basta. Nineteenth century nationalists made him the symbol of the union and of Greater Romania.
sum: Michael the Brave was prince of Wallachia from 1593 to 1601, who briefly ruled Wallachia, Transylvania and Moldavia together in 1600, the first time the three lands later forming Romania had one ruler.
